evals.name: check-only-verifies-observer-prereqs-no-writes
evals.expected_output: Runs the read-only check: probes Python 3.10+, jq, and the claude CLI on PATH as the observer's prerequisites, reports the effective observer userConfig values, flags the --bare/OAuth-auth and idle-threshold hazards, and writes nothing (no settings files, no pluginConfigs). Notes that only the observer has prerequisites and the other session-flow skills are zero-config.
expectations: Probes Python 3.10+, jq, and the claude CLI as the observer's prerequisites
Reports the effective observer userConfig values without editing settings files or pluginConfigs
Flags observer_analysis_bare on an OAuth-login install and observer_idle_seconds below the longest single turn
Scopes setup to the observer only and treats the other skills as zero-config

evals.name: observer-findings-route-to-native-configure
evals.prompt: /session-flow:setup. After the check, how do I apply the observer findings? I want observer_idle_seconds raised.
evals.expected_output: Runs the check, then for each observer finding offers only guidance (install the missing tool, or reconfigure via Claude Code's native /plugin configure session-flow@<marketplace>). It never writes pluginConfigs, mutates user settings, or edits the installed plugin cache, and it does not put observer_idle_seconds into docs/conventions/session-flow.yaml, whose schema does not list it.
expectations: Runs the check before offering any resolution
Routes the observer change to /plugin configure session-flow@<marketplace>, never writing pluginConfigs or user settings
Does not write observer_idle_seconds into docs/conventions/session-flow.yaml

evals.name: apply-writes-a-fresh-repository-file
evals.prompt:
/session-flow:setup apply worker_continuation=respawn

[The repository has no docs/conventions/session-flow.yaml yet.]
evals.expected_output: Runs check first, then calls the setup-apply script with worker_continuation=respawn. The script validates the value against the schema and creates docs/conventions/session-flow.yaml holding worker_continuation: respawn. The re-run check reports the value from the file, and the tracked-file pair reports the file as written but untracked, telling the operator to commit it to share it with the team. No other file is written.
expectations: Runs check before writing
Writes only docs/conventions/session-flow.yaml, holding worker_continuation: respawn
Reports the value from the re-run check, not from the write alone
Says the new file is untracked and must be committed to reach the team, rather than reporting plain success

evals.name: apply-shows-the-diff-before-changing-an-existing-file
evals.prompt:
/session-flow:setup apply worker_continuation=resume

[docs/conventions/session-flow.yaml already exists and holds worker_continuation: respawn under a comment line.]
evals.expected_output: The first script call exits 3 and prints a unified diff from worker_continuation: respawn to worker_continuation: resume without writing. The skill shows that diff and asks the operator whether to write it, then stops for the answer. It re-runs with --yes only after an explicit yes; the comment line stays in the file.
expectations: Shows the diff from respawn to resume before anything is written
Asks for confirmation and does not pass --yes in the same turn as showing the diff
Does not treat the original apply request as confirmation of the diff
Leaves the file unchanged when the operator has not said yes

evals.name: apply-refuses-an-invalid-value
evals.expected_output: The script refuses worker_continuation=restart because it is not resume or respawn, exits 1 and writes nothing. The skill reports the key, the rejected value and the two allowed values, and offers to write one of them instead; it does not write restart by hand or create the file some other way.
expectations: Names worker_continuation, the rejected value restart, and the allowed values resume and respawn
Writes no file, by the script or by hand
Offers a valid value instead of persisting the invalid one

evals.name: check-warns-on-an-invalid-repository-file
evals.prompt:
/session-flow:setup

[docs/conventions/session-flow.yaml holds worker_continuation twice, once as resume and once as respawn.]
evals.expected_output: The repository-settings row is a WARN, not a FAIL, quoting the script's line that worker_continuation appears 2 times. The check writes nothing and points at apply, after the duplicate is removed by hand, as the fix.
expectations: Reports the repository settings row as WARN, never FAIL
Quotes the repeated worker_continuation key from the script output
Writes nothing during the check

evals.name: other-skills-stay-zero-config
evals.prompt: /session-flow:setup — also configure handoff and retro while you are here.
evals.expected_output: Scopes setup to the observer's prerequisites. It does not invent a write path for handoff or retro, treats those skills as zero-config, and still writes no settings files.
expectations: Does not write configuration for handoff or retro
States that only the observer has prerequisites
Still writes no settings files or pluginConfigs
